newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros island secessionists reject dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Comoros island secessionists reject dialogue.

text.p: A secessionist leader on the Comoros island of Anjouan has rejected an offer of dialogue with the government, saying authorities are insincere.

Comoro Islands Foreign Minister Mountar Ahmed Charif told diplomats in the Comoros capital on Thursday the government wanted dialogue with a secessionist movement on Anjouan seeking independence or a return to the French fold.

"No dialogue is possible with the Comoran authorities as long as our president (of the secessionist movement) and our brothers are kept behind bars and we are submitted to ferocious repression," Fatima Mkiri Wa Djimwa told Reuters late on Thursday. She added that the government's appeal was insincere.

Authorities imposed a curfew on the Anjouan capital Mutsamudu on Monday after clashes between security forces and secessionists in which many were reported wounded. Clashes continued until Thursday, witnesses said.
The secessionists were protesting against the arrest on Monday of their leader Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, now replaced by Djimwa.

The Comoro Islands have a population of 190,000 and became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, the second island, argue that independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups.
Djimwa reminded France of its commitment to Anjouan after a statement by France this week denouncing the secessionists and saying it respected the Comoro Islands' integrity.

"Our demand to be re-attached to France may seem (strange) to many across the world but let me tell you...that it is not a politically calculated measure but a feeling which is deeply rooted in my people," she said.
Three people including a gendarme were killed on Anjouan on July 14 in clashes involving secessionists who tried to raise French flags on Bastille Day. Several people were killed in clashes in March.
